evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.field: 形義通解; bronze forms; Shuowen and Guangyun entries
evidence.text: This source proposes that bronze 次 shows an open-mouthed person and two marks interpreted cautiously as saliva; it may be an early form of 咨, with an original sense of consulting or deliberating. It reports that in late Spring and Autumn forms the two marks move below 欠 or become short horizontal strokes, and that Chu slips sometimes use 次 for 即 or 節. Its reading of the marks and original sense is an interpretation, not an established fact. It also gives the Shuowen account 不前不精也。从欠，二聲 and Guangyun fanqie 七四切.
evidence.kind: modern paleographic analysis and historical dictionary record
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 次

evidence.field: character evolution and cited inscription inventory
evidence.text: The page lists oracle-bone examples including 合7361 and 合5814, Western Zhou bronze examples including 集成1354 (史次鼎), and later bronze, Qin slip, seal, clerical and regular-script examples. Its analysis treats the oracle graph as a composite indicator: a component identified as 師’s initial form plus two strokes indicating a military encampment; it describes later bronze forms as 欠 plus 二 phonetic. This conflicts with CUHK’s interpretation of the bronze points as saliva and with accounts rejecting 二 as the original part.
evidence.kind: paleographic reference and interpretation
evidence.title: 次字形演变字源

evidence.field: 字形; historical semantic account; 声系
evidence.text: This dictionary interprets the graph as a person sighing or lamenting, with escaping breath; it rejects 二 as a component of the original graph and says the Shuowen definition and analysis are unclear. It suggests later ‘second/order’ senses may derive from repetition and treats the military lodging sense as use by sound of a graph associated with a military station. These are dictionary proposals; the semantic bridges are not demonstrated in this entry. It records later meanings including lament, consultation, succession/order, lodging and encampment.
evidence.kind: historical lexicographic analysis
evidence.title: 次(ジ)とは？ 意味や使い方 — コトバンク

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.field: dated textual attestations and semantic development
evidence.text: The entry cites Warring States bamboo slips and Han silk manuscripts for ‘inferior/next in rank’ or ‘in sequence’: Shuihudi Qin slips, 語書 slip 8, give 以次傳; Mawangdui Laozi A, line 124 (Han manuscript), repeats 其次 for successive ranks. It separately reports a Han silk use written 次 for 恣 (‘indulge’) and a Mawangdui Xici use written 次 where the transmitted Zhouyi has 濟, presenting these as graphic loans/usages, not stages of the graph’s formation. It cites Zuozhuan 僖公元年 for troops lodging at 聶北 and Zhouli 掌次 for temporary tents, but gives no date for those transmitted textual witnesses in the entry. It traces ordered/serial senses with later literary examples (Liu Yuxi and Bai Juyi) without establishing a precise first occurrence.
evidence.kind: historical sense attestations and dictionary analysis
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 次

evidence.field: Glyph origin; historical pronunciation; modern readings
evidence.text: The entry reports a recent proposal attributed to Zhang (2024): bronze graphic connections with 即 may support an Old Chinese initial *tsʰ-, with a tentative reconstruction /*tsʰik-s/. It says older proposals connecting 次 with 二 (*njis ‘two’), including Pulleyblank (1962) and Sagart and Baxter (2012), are untenable in light of paleographic evidence. This is a secondary summary of a disputed proposal, not direct inspection of Zhang’s article. The entry gives Standard Mandarin cì (Pinyin) and Cantonese ci3 (Jyutping); another entry page lists Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese /*[s-n̥]i[j]-s/ and Zhengzhang /*sn̥ʰis/ for 次, illustrating disagreement among reconstruction systems. No proposed component pronunciation needs to be asserted here because the phonetic status of 二 is contested.
evidence.kind: secondary summary of disputed paleographic and phonological analyses
evidence.title: 次 — Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.field: Japanese reading and word history
evidence.text: The entry identifies Japanese つぎ (tsugi) as a nominalization of the continuative form of 次ぐ (tsugu, ‘follow; be next’), and gives Tokyo pronunciation [tsɨɡʲi]. This supports a Japanese word-history account, not a Japanese origin for the Chinese graph. No early Japanese attestation was verified in the inspected material.
evidence.kind: lexical and pronunciation record
